frenchCards.french: Pourriez-vous m'apporter l'addition, s'il vous plaît ?
frenchCards.note: Polite vous request replacing usted ¿Puede traerme la cuenta? M' is me before a vowel.

frenchCards.french: Pouvez-vous me donner un verre d'eau ?
frenchCards.note: Present-tense polite request. Pourriez-vous is softer and is used elsewhere.

frenchCards.french: Pourriez-vous m'apporter encore de la crème, s'il vous plaît ?
frenchCards.note: Encore = more, matching 'more cream'. Un peu plus de would mean 'a little more', so it is rejected.

frenchCards.french: Pourriez-vous patienter un instant, s'il vous plaît ?
frenchCards.note: Patienter = to wait; un instant = a moment.
Not a literal imperative. Gardez la monnaie is a vous imperative; this phrase is preferred for politeness. Inequivalence: 'Keep the change' used as a tip. Native review open.

frenchVerbParadigms.explanation: Irregular in French. Pourriez-vous (conditional) is the softer polite request used in the lesson. Inequivalence: Spanish stem change vs. French suppletive forms.
Regular -er verb meaning 'to bring'. The Spanish irregular yo form (traigo) has no French counterpart. Used in polite requests with m' (me) before the verb.
Regular -er verb meaning 'to give'. Spanish dar's irregular yo form (doy) does not carry over.
Stem change in the singular and ils forms (paie/paient). Spelling variant je paye also exists; paie is used here. Payer par carte / en espèces mirrors pagar con tarjeta / en efectivo.

Quedarse con (to keep) is reflexive in Spanish; garder is transitive. Inequivalence: 'keep the change' is rendered as Je vous laisse la monnaie, using laisser, not garder. Rester (to stay) is the other meaning of quedarse, not used here.

internalDomainNotes: Setting kept as Oaxaca with 200 pesos; no euro conversion and no France redesign. The draft's Lyon/euros variant was not used.
Cream (la crème) and tip (le pourboire) are preserved, not silently replaced.
'Keep the change' is rendered as Je vous laisse la monnaie, a polite phrase rather than a literal vous imperative. Gardez la monnaie is a valid alternative but not used.
All address is vouvoiement (vous, Pourriez-vous, Pouvez-vous) to match the polite usted register.
Source objective contains 'bill' and 'check' for the same item; both map to l'addition. No duplicate card created.
Progression: term meaning (tip, change) -> phrase translation (bill, water, keep change) -> reader line (200 pesos) -> speaking objective.
Speaking objective is source-verbatim; French speaking practice uses polite requests and je vous laisse la monnaie.
residuals: Native French review is open for Je vous laisse la monnaie as a tipping phrase.
Inequivalence: 'Keep the change' (imperative in English) is rendered as a polite statement, not a literal command.
Inequivalence: 'the straw' (popote, Mexican) maps to la paille, the standard French term; regional difference noted.
Inequivalence: 'the card' maps to la carte bancaire to avoid the menu meaning of la carte.
Inequivalence: 'more cream' uses encore de la crème; un peu plus de was rejected because it means 'a little more'.
Source objective says 'usted commands'; French uses polite vous questions instead, so the command register is not preserved literally.
Ice mapping: les glaçons (ice cubes) is the closest French match to hielo in 'agua con hielo'; ice in general would be la glace.
Setting and currency remain source-anchored (Oaxaca, 200 pesos); no conversion applied.
